units.translation: We said above that the particle γάρ [for] is never placed at the beginning of a sentence, but is usually attached to the first or second word, and indeed it is very often attached to the second when it is closely connected with the first, as ὁ μὲν γάρ [for he on the one hand], ἐφ᾽ οἷς γάρ [for on which], and the rest of this kind, especially after nouns with articles. Thus τὸ σὸν γὰρ ἄνθος [for your flower] Pr. 7. ὁ λωφήσων γὰρ [for the one who will relieve] 27. τὰν Διὸς γὰρ [for the of Zeus] 905. τούς προδότας γὰρ [for the traitors] 1068. τὸν φθίμενον γάρ [for the dead man] Sept. 336. τὰ δεσποτῶν γὰρ [for the masters'] Ag. 32. τῶν πολυκτόνων γὰρ [for the murderous] 461. τὸ δυσσεβὲς γὰρ [for the impious] 758. τὴν κάτω γὰρ [for the below] 871. τὸ μόρσιμον γὰρ [for the fated] Ch. 103. τοὺς φιλτάτους γὰρ [for the dearest] 234. τὰ πάντα γὰρ [for all things] 520. τοῖς σώφροσιν γὰρ [for the prudent] Eum. 136. οὑπιρρέων γὰρ [for the one flowing upon] 853. τοῦ γηγενούς γάρ [for the earth-born] Suppl. 250. τοῖς ἥσσοσιν γὰρ [for the weaker] 489. ὁ μὲν γάρ [for he on the one hand] Sept. 511. Ag. 1630. οἱ μὲν γὰρ [for they on the one hand] 326. τοὶ μὲν γὰρ [for these on the one hand] Sept. 295. οὓς μὲν γὰρ [for whom on the one hand] Ag. 433. τὰ μὲν γὰρ [for these things on the one hand] 1056. Ch. 278 748. Eum. 222. εἰ μὲν γὰρ [for if on the one hand] Sept. 4. Suppl. 472. ἦν μὲν γὰρ [for there was on the one hand] fr. 178. πρῶτα μὲν γὰρ [for first on the one hand] Pr. 1016. πολλὰ μὲν γὰρ [for many things on the one hand] Pers. 459 707. κρατοῦσα μὲν γὰρ [for ruling on the one hand] Sept. 189. ὅ τε γὰρ [for the and] Ag. 76. θεοῦ τε γὰρ [for and of the god] Sept. 427. λευκοῖς τε γὰρ [for and with white] fr. 114. καὶ παῖδα γάρ [for even a child] Ag. 1040. ἀλλ᾽ εἰσορῶ γὰρ [but for I see] Pr. 941. ἀλλὰ διπλῆς γαρ [but for of double] Ch. 375. ἐκ τοῦ γὰρ [for from this] Ag. 1478. ἐν ἀγγέλῳ γὰρ [for in a messenger] Ch. 773. ἐφ᾽ ἄρματος γὰρ [for on a chariot] fr. 32. ἀπὸ στρατείας γὰρ [for from an expedition] Eum. 631. κατ᾿ ἀρχῆς γὰρ [for from the beginning] Suppl. 485. τίν᾿ ἀνδρῶν γὰρ [for which of men] Sept. 771. χάριν τροφᾶς γὰρ [for thanks for nurture] Ag. 729. μόνος θεῶν γὰρ [for alone of the gods] fr. 156. θεὸς θεῶν γὰρ [for god of gods] Pr. 29. βροτοὺς θρασύνει γὰρ [for it emboldens mortals] Ag. 222. In fourth position is placed ἀλλ᾽ ἐκ Διὸς γὰρ [but for from Zeus] Eum. 797. τὸ μὴ θέμις γὰρ [for what is not lawful] Ch. 641. τὸ μὴ φρονοῦν γὰρ [for what is not thinking] 753.

When γάρ [for] is combined with other particles, it either precedes them, as γὰρ δή [for indeed] and γὰρ οὖν [for therefore], or follows them, as ἀλλὰ γάρ [but for], καὶ γάρ [and for], μὲν γάρ [on the one hand for], τοι γάρ [indeed for], about which it has been said in their own places.
Sending an army for Helen's sake—for I will not conceal it from you—you were very unmusically written.
But I, for I pity him, will not be angry.
But to me, for the gods have brought necessity that surrounds the city; for from the house ...
I will speak, for you command it, the word from my heart.
And now Orestes, for he was well-aimed, carrying out ...
But I, for my mother's blood drives me, will pursue justice.
And indeed, for I love these things, and they are not loathsome to me.
For you will not persuade him at all; for he is not easily persuaded.
HD. Always indeed you are pitiless and full of boldness. KR. For there is no remedy in lamenting this man in vain.
Why do you hate it (the art)? For the art is not to blame for any of the toils.
For there were beds of enemies near the walls; for from heaven and from earth meadowy dews were sprinkling down
